name: UK energy price cap
summary: Cap £1,723; January forecasts range from Cornwall Insight's £1,999 to suppliers' £2,250; a 20%-plus rise is unconfirmed
state: Ofgem's cap for October to December is £1,723 a year for a typical dual-fuel household. Cornwall Insight's latest forecast found, on a page updated 14 Oct, puts January at about £1,999, about 16% higher. Supplier forecasts collated by MoneySavingExpert, updated 3 Nov, are higher, at £2,193 to £2,250, up 27% to 31%, and it labels them weak predictions. A rise of 20% or more would cross the Alert line, but it rests on that single source and Cornwall's newer figure could not be found on 8 Nov, so the Alert is unconfirmed.
for_you: Households on default tariffs pay at the cap rate, and those with high winter gas use or on prepayment meters are most exposed to a January rise. The figure depends on wholesale prices up to 18 Nov.
rubric_hit: Watch: cap £1,723 in £1,700–2,200 band; Cornwall forecast +16% above the 5% line. Alert line of a 20% forecast rise is met only by supplier forecasts on one site, so unconfirmed.
